-- Per-type exclusions: some prop keys exist on multiple types but make sense to randomize on
-- only one. Trail's logical `Duration` (TypeRegistry attrName=EmitDuration) is rolled here
-- only when the type is Trail; non-Trail items use the virtual `EmitDuration` instead.
RandomizerRules.typeExcludes = {
	-- Trail items skip the virtual EmitCount/EmitDelay (Trail directAccess; not meaningful).
	Trail = { EmitCount = true, EmitDelay = true, EmitDuration = true },
	-- Non-Trail items skip Trail's directAccess `Duration` logical prop (Trail-only).
	Part = { Duration = true }, Beam = { Duration = true }, PointLight = { Duration = true },
	Highlight = { Duration = true },
	Attachment = { Duration = true }, Model = { Duration = true },
	Lightning = { Duration = true },
	CameraShake = { Duration = true },
	Sound = { Duration = true },
	Rocks = { Duration = true },
	Rope = { Duration = true },
	-- Resolution is a perf knob, not an aesthetic - rolling it would silently
	-- rebuild the shared canvas at random cost.
	Distortion = { Duration = true, Resolution = true },
}

-- Cross-type excludes  -  props that exist on multiple types but never make sense to
-- randomize. AccelerationTowardsInstance is a boolean gate that depends on AccelTarget
-- being a valid Instance picked by the user; flipping it on without a target rolls
-- nothing useful, and rolling it off discards the user's setup. Strength still rolls.
RandomizerRules.globalExcludes = {
	AccelerationTowardsInstance = true,
	-- Behavior flags (scale-propagation gates), authored intentionally — not rolled.
	ScaleMotion = true,
	ScaleRotation = true,
	-- Rocks/Rope Gravity sign/magnitude is too semantic to roll (196.2 = Roblox default).
	Gravity = true,
	SinkOut = true,
	InheritFloor = true,
	-- Rope structure: pinning, auto-length, motion aim, lifecycle are authored
	-- intent, not variety.
	PinMode = true,
	RopeLength = true,
	MotionTarget = true,
	SpawnTarget = true,
	DeathMode = true,
	DeathWindow = true,
	-- Lightning Seek retarget flicker is authored intent.
	SeekRetarget = true,
	-- Distortion structure: field/epicenter selection + the overdrive safety gate
	-- are authored intent; Amplify rides an engine bug and must never self-arm.
	FieldKind = true,
	EpicenterMode = true,
	Amplify = true,
	AllowOverdrive = true,
}

-- =========================================================
-- DERIVE  -  hybrid override + auto
-- =========================================================

-- Build a fresh rule from override bounds + propDef.type-driven shape. virtualEmitAttr is
-- a special case: scalar + integer regardless of propDef (not in TypeRegistry).
local function _decorateOverride(override, propDef)
	-- virtualEmitAttr: scalar shape, copy bounds + integer flag.
	if override.virtualEmitAttr then
		return {
			scalar = true,
			min = override.min, max = override.max,
			integer = override.integer,
			perfSensitive = override.perfSensitive,
			virtualEmitAttr = true,
		}
	end
	-- No propDef means caller passed a key not in TypeRegistry (e.g. raw PE prop). Without
	-- shape info, can't dispatch a generator. Skip.
	if not propDef then return nil end

	local nn = propDef.nonNegative or false
	-- Resolve effective bounds: override wins if present, otherwise nonNegative-aware default.
	-- nonNegative ALWAYS clamps lo to >= 0 even when override has a negative min  -  otherwise
	-- TypeRegistry.write would silently clamp the value post-roll, collapsing rolls toward 0
	-- and skewing the expected distribution.
	local lo = override.min if lo == nil then lo = nn and 0 or -10 end
	if nn and lo < 0 then lo = 0 end
	local hi = override.max if hi == nil then hi = 10 end
	local rule = {
		min = lo, max = hi,
		integer = override.integer,
		perfSensitive = override.perfSensitive,
	}
	-- Shape comes from propDef.type at THIS type. Same logical prop key can be different
	-- shapes across types (Brightness is NumberSequence on Beam, scalar `number` on Trail).
	local t = propDef.type
	if t == "boolean" then return {coin = true} end
	if t == "enum" then return nil end -- skip uncurated enums
	if t == "ColorSequence" then return {colorSequence = true} end
	if t == "NumberSequence" then
		rule.numberSequence = true
		rule.minKeypoints = override.minKeypoints or 3
		rule.maxKeypoints = override.maxKeypoints or 7
		return rule
	end
	if t == "NumberRange" then rule.numberRange = true; return rule end
	if t == "number" then rule.scalar = true; return rule end
	if t == "Vector3" then return {vector = true, axes = 3, min = lo, max = hi} end
	if t == "Vector2" then return {vector = true, axes = 2, min = lo, max = hi} end
	if t == "UDim2" then return {udim2 = true} end
	-- Anything else (string asset IDs, instance refs, custom types): skip.
	return nil
end

-- Pure-auto fallback when no override exists. Uses propDef.type + nonNegative.
local function _autoFromPropDef(propDef)
	if not propDef then return nil end
	if propDef.type == "boolean" then return {coin = true} end
	if propDef.type == "enum" then return nil end -- skip uncurated
	if propDef.type == "ColorSequence" then return {colorSequence = true} end
	local nn = propDef.nonNegative or false
	if propDef.type == "NumberSequence" then
		return {numberSequence = true, min = nn and 0 or -10, max = 10, minKeypoints = 3, maxKeypoints = 7}
	end
	if propDef.type == "NumberRange" then
		return {numberRange = true, min = nn and 0 or -10, max = 10}
	end
	if propDef.type == "number" then
		return {scalar = true, min = nn and 0 or -10, max = 10}
	end
	if propDef.type == "Vector3" then return {vector = true, axes = 3, min = -10, max = 10} end
	if propDef.type == "Vector2" then return {vector = true, axes = 2, min = -10, max = 10} end
	if propDef.type == "UDim2" then return {udim2 = true} end
	return nil
end

-- Native PE prop type map. Values mirror Roblox ParticleEmitter property types.
-- Used by derive("PE", ...) to build a rule when propDef is nil (PE has no
-- TypeRegistry entry). Boolean props omitted  -  PE booleans aren't randomization-
-- friendly (WindAffectsDrag, FlipbookBlendFrames). Emit timing attrs route through
-- the existing virtualEmitAttr path on the item itself.
local PE_PROP_TYPES = {
	Rate = "scalarPos",                 -- 0..50
	Lifetime = "numberRange",            -- (lo, hi)
	SpreadAngle = "vector2",             -- degrees
	EmitCount = "scalarPosInt",          -- 0..50
	EmitDelay = "scalarNonNeg",          -- 0..2
	EmitDuration = "scalarNonNeg",       -- 0..3
	Brightness = "scalarPos",            -- 0..2
	Size = "numberSequence",
	Transparency = "numberSequence",
	Color = "colorSequence",
	Squash = "numberSequence",
	LightEmission = "scalarUnit",        -- 0..1
	LightInfluence = "scalarUnit",       -- 0..1
	ZOffset = "scalarSym",               -- -2..2
	Speed = "numberRange",
	RotSpeed = "numberRange",
	Rotation = "numberRange",
	Acceleration = "vector3",
	Drag = "scalarNonNeg",               -- 0..3
	VelocityInheritance = "scalarUnit",  -- 0..1
	TimeScale = "scalarPos",             -- 0..2
	FlipbookFramerate = "numberRange",   -- Roblox PE FlipbookFramerate is NumberRange.
}

-- Per-PE-prop bound overrides. Generic kind defaults (numberRange 0..5,
-- numberSequence 0..1) are too tight for properties whose native Roblox scale
-- is much larger (Rotation/RotSpeed in degrees, Squash -10..10, Speed 0..50).
local PE_BOUNDS = {
	-- numberRange (Vector2 keypoint pair)  -  explicit min/max in property's native units.
	Speed = {min = 0, max = 50},
	RotSpeed = {min = -360, max = 360},
	Rotation = {min = 0, max = 360},
	Lifetime = {min = 0.1, max = 5},
	-- numberSequence  -  Squash is signed -10..10; Size typical visual range.
	Size = {min = 0.5, max = 5},
	Squash = {min = -10, max = 10},
	-- scalarPos overrides
	Rate = {min = 1, max = 80},
	FlipbookFramerate = {min = 1, max = 60},
	Brightness = {min = 0, max = 100},
	-- scalarUnit overrides  -  both clamped to native PE's accepted [0,1] range.
	-- LightInfluence: probability=0.25 → 25% chance to roll a value, 75% chance
	-- to commit 0. Matches plugin convention that most randomized PEs render unlit.
	-- LightEmission is scalarUnit per PE_PROP_TYPES; Roblox clamps to [0,1]
	-- internally so any non-unit override would silently snap.
	LightEmission = {min = 0, max = 1},
	LightInfluence = {min = 0, max = 1, probability = 0.25},
	-- SpreadAngle is the size of a random emission spread; negative components
	-- are not meaningful. Cap each component at [0, 360].
	SpreadAngle = {vector = true, axes = 2, min = 0, max = 360},
}

local function _peRule(propKey)
	local kind = PE_PROP_TYPES[propKey]
	if not kind then return nil end
	local override = PE_BOUNDS[propKey]
	local rule
	if kind == "scalarPos" then
		local hi = override and override.max or ((propKey == "Rate" or propKey == "FlipbookFramerate") and 30 or 2)
		local lo = override and override.min or 0
		rule = {scalar = true, min = lo, max = hi}
	elseif kind == "scalarPosInt" then rule = {scalar = true, min = 0, max = 50, integer = true}
	elseif kind == "scalarNonNeg" then rule = {scalar = true, min = 0, max = 3}
	elseif kind == "scalarUnit" then
		local lo = override and override.min or 0
		local hi = override and override.max or 1
		rule = {scalar = true, min = lo, max = hi, probability = override and override.probability}
	elseif kind == "scalarSym" then rule = {scalar = true, min = -2, max = 2}
	elseif kind == "numberRange" then
		local lo = override and override.min or 0
		local hi = override and override.max or 5
		rule = {numberRange = true, min = lo, max = hi}
	elseif kind == "vector2" then
		-- Respect PE_BOUNDS override so SpreadAngle (and any future per-prop
		-- vector2 with custom range) isn't stuck on the generic [-180, 180].
		local lo = override and override.min or -180
		local hi = override and override.max or 180
		rule = {vector = true, axes = 2, min = lo, max = hi}
	elseif kind == "vector3" then rule = {vector = true, axes = 3, min = -10, max = 10}
	elseif kind == "numberSequence" then
		local lo = override and override.min or 0
		local hi = override and override.max or 1
		rule = {numberSequence = true, min = lo, max = hi}
	elseif kind == "colorSequence" then rule = {colorSequence = true}
	end
	if rule then rule.nativePE = true end
	-- Emit timing attrs go through the item-level setattribute path, not native property.
	if propKey == "EmitCount" or propKey == "EmitDelay" or propKey == "EmitDuration" then
		rule.virtualEmitAttr = true
		rule.nativePE = nil
	end
	return rule
end

-- Per-type-and-name overrides for props whose native scale differs by type. Beats
-- byName for the matching (typeName, propKey). E.g. ColorCorrection.Brightness is
-- signed -1..1 (Roblox native), not the 0..2 PointLight-suitable byName default.
RandomizerRules.byTypeAndName = {
	ColorCorrection = {
		Brightness = {min = -1, max = 1, minKeypoints = 3, maxKeypoints = 7},
		Contrast = {min = -1, max = 1, minKeypoints = 3, maxKeypoints = 7},
		Saturation = {min = -1, max = 1, minKeypoints = 3, maxKeypoints = 7},
	},
	Atmosphere = {
		Density = {min = 0, max = 1, minKeypoints = 3, maxKeypoints = 7},
		Offset = {min = 0, max = 1, minKeypoints = 3, maxKeypoints = 7},
		Glare = {min = 0, max = 24, minKeypoints = 3, maxKeypoints = 7},
		Haze = {min = 0, max = 10, minKeypoints = 3, maxKeypoints = 7},
	},
	Distortion = {
		-- byName Amplitude is Lightning-curated (0.05-0.4, below this type's 0.5
		-- default); byName Speed is Part-curated studs/s (-20..50). Distortion
		-- Amplitude authors ~0..1 slope units, Speed a friendly signed 1-10.
		Amplitude = {min = 0.1, max = 1, minKeypoints = 2, maxKeypoints = 5},
		Speed = {min = -8, max = 8},
	},
}

function RandomizerRules.derive(typeName, propKey, propDef)
	-- Cross-type exclude pre-check (applies before PE / per-type filters).
	if RandomizerRules.globalExcludes[propKey] then return nil end
	-- Native PE rules  -  PE has no TypeRegistry entry, so derive consults a hardcoded
	-- type map keyed off the prop name.
	if typeName == "PE" then return _peRule(propKey) end
	-- Per-type exclude pre-check.
	local excludes = RandomizerRules.typeExcludes[typeName]
	if excludes and excludes[propKey] then return nil end

	-- Trail Duration special case: TypeData stores it as type="string" (range format
	-- "min, max" parsed by the directAccess Trail readers). Generic derive would skip
	-- strings. Roll a scalar in [0, 3] and writer tostring-wraps before TypeRegistry.
	-- write. Trail items show Duration; non-Trail show virtual EmitDuration.
	if typeName == "Trail" and propKey == "Duration" then
		return {scalar = true, min = 0, max = 3, perfSensitive = true, stringForm = true}
	end

	-- Type-specific override beats byName.
	local typeOverrides = RandomizerRules.byTypeAndName[typeName]
	local override = typeOverrides and typeOverrides[propKey] or RandomizerRules.byName[propKey]
	if override then return _decorateOverride(override, propDef) end

	-- No override: pure auto-derive from propDef.type.
	return _autoFromPropDef(propDef)
end

-- =========================================================
-- GENERATORS
-- =========================================================

-- Scalar (number)
function RandomizerRules.rollScalar(rule)
	-- Probability gate: PE LightInfluence rolls a value 25% of the time and 0
	-- otherwise so most randomized PEs render unlit (matches plugin convention).
	if rule.probability and math.random() > rule.probability then
		return 0
	end
	local lo, hi = rule.min or 0, rule.max or 1
	if rule.integer then return math.random(math.floor(lo), math.floor(hi)) end
	return lo + math.random() * (hi - lo)
end

-- NumberRange (min/max pair, sorted)
function RandomizerRules.rollNumberRange(rule)
	local lo, hi = rule.min or 0, rule.max or 1
	local a = lo + math.random() * (hi - lo)
	local b = lo + math.random() * (hi - lo)
	if a > b then a, b = b, a end
	return NumberRange.new(a, b)
end

-- NumberSequence  -  keypoint count depends on the rule.randomizeKeypoints flag:
--   OFF (default): exactly 2 keypoints (t=0 + t=1) with random values + envelopes  -  gives
--                  a simple start/end envelope-style randomization.
--   ON: 3..7 keypoints, sorted random times, bounded envelopes  -  produces a varied shape.
function RandomizerRules.rollNumberSequence(rule)
	local minKp, maxKp
	if rule.randomizeKeypoints then
		minKp = rule.minKeypoints or 3
		maxKp = rule.maxKeypoints or 7
	else
		minKp, maxKp = 2, 2
	end
	local n = math.random(minKp, maxKp)
	-- Times: anchor 0 and 1, n-2 random ascending in between.
	local times = {0}
	for i = 1, n - 2 do table.insert(times, math.random()) end
	table.insert(times, 1)
	table.sort(times)
	local lo, hi = rule.min or 0, rule.max or 1
	local rangeSpan = hi - lo
	local kps = {}
	for _, t in ipairs(times) do
		local v = lo + math.random() * rangeSpan
		if rule.integer then v = math.floor(v + 0.5) end
		-- Envelope clamped so value +/- envelope stays within [lo, hi]. 0..50% of remaining
		-- headroom  -  full envelope-to-edge would saturate at the bounds and look ugly.
		local headroom = math.min(v - lo, hi - v)
		local env = math.random() * headroom * 0.5
		if rule.integer then env = math.floor(env + 0.5) end
		table.insert(kps, NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(t, v, env))
	end
	return NumberSequence.new(kps)
end

-- Color (single Color3, vivid)
function RandomizerRules.rollColor()
	local h = math.random()
	local s = 0.6 + math.random() * 0.4
	local v = 0.5 + math.random() * 0.5
	return Color3.fromHSV(h, s, v)
end

-- ColorSequence  -  algorithmic palette. Picks a mode (weighted) and produces
-- 2 keypoints (when randomizeKeypoints OFF) or 3..6 keypoints (when ON), each color
-- sampled by the palette's hue rule via PALETTE_SAMPLERS below.
local COLOR_MODES = {
	{name = "Analogous",     weight = 3},
	{name = "Complementary", weight = 2},
	{name = "Monochrome",    weight = 2},
	{name = "Warm",          weight = 1},
	{name = "Cool",          weight = 1},
	{name = "WhiteToColor",  weight = 1},
}

local function pickColorMode()
	local total = 0
	for _, m in ipairs(COLOR_MODES) do total = total + m.weight end
	local r = math.random() * total
	local acc = 0
	for _, m in ipairs(COLOR_MODES) do
		acc = acc + m.weight
		if r <= acc then return m.name end
	end
	return COLOR_MODES[1].name
end

local function hsv(h, s, v) return Color3.fromHSV(h % 1, math.clamp(s, 0, 1), math.clamp(v, 0, 1)) end

-- Per-row palette dropdown lets the user pin the algorithmic palette mode for
-- ColorSequence rolls instead of the weighted random `pickColorMode`. UI sends the
-- chosen mode as `rule.paletteMode` (string: Auto / Analogous / Complementary /
-- Monochrome / Warm / Cool / WhiteToColor); "Auto" / nil falls back to weighted random.
RandomizerRules.PALETTE_MODES = {"Auto", "Analogous", "Complementary", "Monochrome", "Warm", "Cool", "WhiteToColor"}

-- Validate modeOverride against PALETTE_MODES. Unknown strings (typo, stale saved
-- setting, future-version mode the current build doesn't know) get reset to nil so
-- the call falls through to weighted-random pickColorMode() rather than silently
-- using the PALETTE_SAMPLERS WhiteToColor fallback. PALETTE_MODE_SET is O(1) lookup.
local PALETTE_MODE_SET = {}
for _, name in ipairs(RandomizerRules.PALETTE_MODES) do PALETTE_MODE_SET[name] = true end

-- Per-palette samplers  -  each returns a Color3 honoring the palette's hue rule.
-- baseHue + i (0-based) + n let some palettes alternate (Complementary, WhiteToColor)
-- while others sample-with-jitter (Analogous, Monochrome, Warm, Cool).
local PALETTE_SAMPLERS = {
	Analogous = function(baseHue, _i, _n)
		local drift = (math.random() - 0.5) * 0.32  -- ±0.16 around baseHue
		return hsv(baseHue + drift, 0.6 + math.random() * 0.25, 0.8 + math.random() * 0.15)
	end,
	Complementary = function(baseHue, i, _n)
		local h = ((i % 2) == 0) and baseHue or (baseHue + 0.5) % 1
		return hsv(h, 0.65 + math.random() * 0.2, 0.85 + math.random() * 0.1)
	end,
	Monochrome = function(baseHue, _i, _n)
		return hsv(baseHue, 0.5 + math.random() * 0.4, 0.4 + math.random() * 0.55)
	end,
	Warm = function(_baseHue, _i, _n)
		return hsv(math.random() * 0.2, 0.7 + math.random() * 0.2, 0.85 + math.random() * 0.1)
	end,
	Cool = function(_baseHue, _i, _n)
		return hsv(0.45 + math.random() * 0.25, 0.7 + math.random() * 0.2, 0.85 + math.random() * 0.1)
	end,
	WhiteToColor = function(baseHue, i, _n)
		if (i % 2) == 0 then return Color3.new(1, 1, 1) end
		return hsv(baseHue, 0.7 + math.random() * 0.2, 0.85 + math.random() * 0.1)
	end,
}

-- ColorSequence roller supports both OFF (2 keypoints) and ON (3..6 keypoints) keypoint
-- counts AND honors the palette mode in either case. ON + explicit palette (Warm / Cool
-- / etc.) samples multi-keypoint colors within the palette's hue family; ON + Auto
-- picks a palette via weighted random first. OFF
-- mirrors that with exactly 2 keypoints  -  palette still constrains the start/end.
function RandomizerRules.rollColorSequence(modeOverride, randomizeKeypoints)
	if modeOverride and not PALETTE_MODE_SET[modeOverride] then modeOverride = nil end
	local mode = (modeOverride and modeOverride ~= "Auto" and modeOverride) or pickColorMode()
	local sampler = PALETTE_SAMPLERS[mode] or PALETTE_SAMPLERS.WhiteToColor
	local n = randomizeKeypoints and math.random(3, 6) or 2
	local times
	if n == 2 then
		times = {0, 1}
	else
		times = {0}
		for _ = 1, n - 2 do table.insert(times, math.random()) end
		table.insert(times, 1)
		table.sort(times)
	end
	local baseHue = math.random()
	local kps = {}
	for i, t in ipairs(times) do
		table.insert(kps, ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(t, sampler(baseHue, i - 1, n)))
	end
	return ColorSequence.new(kps)
end

-- Vector (Vector2 / Vector3)
function RandomizerRules.rollVector(rule)
	local axes = rule.axes or 3
	local lo, hi = rule.min or -10, rule.max or 10
	local span = hi - lo
	if axes == 2 then
		return Vector2.new(lo + math.random() * span, lo + math.random() * span)
	end
	return Vector3.new(lo + math.random() * span, lo + math.random() * span, lo + math.random() * span)
end

-- UDim2  -  random scale + offset within sane UI ranges. Plugin uses UDim2 for ImageLabel
-- positioning; offset 0..200 px, scale 0..1.
function RandomizerRules.rollUDim2()
	return UDim2.new(math.random(), math.random(0, 200), math.random(), math.random(0, 200))
end

-- Boolean (coin)
function RandomizerRules.rollBoolean()
	return math.random() < 0.5
end

-- Enum: caller passes an enum profile (curated subset of valid Enum.X.Name strings).
function RandomizerRules.rollEnum(profile)
	if not profile or #profile == 0 then return nil end
	return profile[math.random(1, #profile)]
end

-- =========================================================
-- ROLL DISPATCH (rule -> generator)
-- =========================================================

-- Single entry point: callers pass a rule from RandomizerRules.derive() + optional context.
-- Returns the generated value, or nil if rule shape is unrecognized.
function RandomizerRules.roll(rule)
	if not rule then return nil end
	if rule.coin then return RandomizerRules.rollBoolean() end
	if rule.colorSequence then return RandomizerRules.rollColorSequence(rule.paletteMode, rule.randomizeKeypoints) end
	if rule.numberSequence then return RandomizerRules.rollNumberSequence(rule) end
	if rule.numberRange then return RandomizerRules.rollNumberRange(rule) end
	if rule.vector then return RandomizerRules.rollVector(rule) end
	if rule.udim2 then return RandomizerRules.rollUDim2() end
	-- Default: scalar (covers `byName` curated bounds and `derive` numeric returns).
	return RandomizerRules.rollScalar(rule)
end

return RandomizerRules

--[[
	RandomizerSection  -  Part-Icles V5 Randomizer System
	Copyright (C) 2026 Qwinkle

	Builds one category section's UI:
	  Header blob: collapse arrow + tristate glyph (none/some/all) + label
	  Body Frame: per-prop rows (label blob + optional palette dropdown + IsOn toggle).

	Caller passes a `bag` of shared state + helpers. We don't capture upvalues from
	RandomizerWiring directly because:
	  - Mutable tables (_checked, _paletteMode, _toggleConns, etc.) share by reference.
	  - Mutable scalars (_lastBatch, _groupAxes) come through getter callbacks so the
	    row closures see the live values from RandomizerWiring's outer scope.

	NOT user-script-reachable. Internal-only.
]]

local M = {}

function M.emit(bag, sec, sectionTypeName, sectionUid, headerText, parent)
	local W = bag.W
	local Th = bag.Th
	local TypeRegistry = bag.TypeRegistry
	local Rules = bag.Rules
	local _checked = bag.checked
	local _paletteMode = bag.paletteMode
	local _itemTypeName = bag.itemTypeName
	local _sectionProps = bag.sectionProps
	local _sectionHeaderRefresh = bag.sectionHeaderRefresh
	local _typeRowToggles = bag.typeRowToggles
	local _typeHeaderRefresh = bag.typeHeaderRefresh
	local _toggleConns = bag.toggleConns
	local AXIS_TO_FAMILY = bag.AXIS_TO_FAMILY
	local _compKey = bag.compKey
	local _hasMixedLinkState = bag.hasMixedLinkState
	local _refreshHeaderGlyph = bag.refreshHeaderGlyph
	local _restoreSnapshots = bag.restoreSnapshots
	local _replayBatch = bag.replayBatch
	local _rollBatch = bag.rollBatch
	local getLastBatch = bag.getLastBatch
	local getGroupAxes = bag.getGroupAxes
	local getResetOnUncheck = bag.getResetOnUncheck
	local getOrInitRetainedBatch = bag.getOrInitRetainedBatch

	-- Header blob (collapse arrow on the left, then tristate glyph, then label).
	local hdr = W.makeBlob("Section_" .. sectionUid, parent, UDim2.new(1, -8, 0, 22))
	W.addPadding(hdr, 4, 4, 0, 0)
	local glyph = Instance.new("TextButton")
	glyph.Name = "Glyph"
	glyph.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	glyph.Text = "[ ]"
	glyph.Font = Th.Font; glyph.TextSize = 11; glyph.TextColor3 = Th.Gold
	glyph.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left
	-- Glyph box trimmed to bracket text width so [ ] sits adjacent to the label.
	glyph.Position = UDim2.new(0, 16, 0, 0); glyph.Size = UDim2.new(0, 16, 1, 0)
	glyph.Parent = hdr
	local label = W.makeLabel("L", hdr, headerText, Th.Gold, Th.Font, 11)
	label.Position = UDim2.new(0, 34, 0, 0)
	label.Size = UDim2.new(1, -38, 1, 0)

	-- Section body holds the per-prop rows; collapse arrow toggles its visibility.
	local sectionBody = Instance.new("Frame")
	sectionBody.Name = "Body_" .. sectionUid
	sectionBody.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	sectionBody.AutomaticSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.Y
	sectionBody.Size = UDim2.new(1, -8, 0, 0)
	sectionBody.Parent = parent
	W.addListLayout(sectionBody, 4, Enum.FillDirection.Vertical)
	W.addCollapseButton(hdr, {sectionBody}, {anchorLeft = true, arrowPos = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 0)})

	-- Cache composite keys + per-header refresh closure.
	local sectionComps = {}
	for _, propKey in ipairs(sec.props) do
		table.insert(sectionComps, _compKey(sectionTypeName, propKey))
	end
	_sectionProps[sectionUid] = sectionComps
	local sectionPropsRef = sec.props
	_sectionHeaderRefresh[sectionUid] = function()
		_refreshHeaderGlyph(sectionUid, glyph)
	end

	local rowToggles = {}
	for _, propKey in ipairs(sec.props) do
		local rowComp = _compKey(sectionTypeName, propKey)
		local row = Instance.new("Frame")
		row.Name = "Row_" .. rowComp
		row.BackgroundTransparency = 1
		row.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 22)
		row.Parent = sectionBody

		-- Label may carry "(mixed link)" qualifier if items in the same type disagree
		-- on whether this axis is linked to a primary.
		local labelText = propKey
		if _hasMixedLinkState(sectionTypeName, propKey) then
			labelText = labelText .. "  (mixed link)"
		end

		-- Row blob spans the full row; toggle (and palette dropdown for ColorSequence
		-- rows) overlay the right end. Probe via Rules.derive so PE Color (no
		-- TypeRegistry entry / no propDef) still surfaces the palette dropdown  -  derive's
		-- PE branch reports colorSequence.
		local typeDef = TypeRegistry.Types[sectionTypeName]
		local pd = typeDef and typeDef.properties and typeDef.properties[propKey]
		local probeRule = Rules.derive(sectionTypeName, propKey, pd)
		local isColorSeq = probeRule and probeRule.colorSequence
		-- Inside-padding right value reserves space for toggle (28w + 4 margin) and
		-- palette dropdown (84w + 8 margin) when present, so text doesn't overlap them.
		local rightPad = isColorSeq and 122 or 34

		local labelBlob = W.makeBlob("LabelBlob_"..rowComp, row, UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, -2))
		labelBlob.Position = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 1)
		W.addPadding(labelBlob, 14, rightPad, 0, 0)
		W.makeLabel("L", labelBlob, labelText, Th.MutedGold, Th.Font, 10)

		if isColorSeq then
			local current = _paletteMode[rowComp] or "Auto"
			local _, dd, setOnChanged = W.makeDropdown(
				"Pal_" .. rowComp, row,
				Rules.PALETTE_MODES, current
			)
			dd.Size = UDim2.new(0, 84, 0, 18)
			dd.Position = UDim2.new(1, -116, 0.5, -9)
			setOnChanged(function(modeName)
				_paletteMode[rowComp] = modeName ~= "Auto" and modeName or nil
				if _checked[rowComp] and getLastBatch() then _rollBatch() end
			end)
		end

		local toggle = W.makeToggle("Rand_" .. rowComp, row)
		toggle.Position = UDim2.new(1, -26, 0.5, -8)
		rowToggles[propKey] = toggle
		table.insert(_typeRowToggles[sectionTypeName], {comp = rowComp, toggle = toggle})

		-- IsOn handler: sync _checked. Uncheck: filter _lastBatch by typeName + matching
		-- origin (same family.primary if grouped, else propKey itself). Reset-on-uncheck
		-- ON: drop entries + restore + replay. OFF: MOVE entries to retained batch  - 
		-- they survive the next Roll's snapshot restore and commit on Apply.
		-- Re-check (on=true): drop matching entries from retained so the next Roll can
		-- generate fresh values without an old retained ghost write fighting them.
		local conn = toggle:GetAttributeChangedSignal("IsOn"):Connect(function()
			local on = toggle:GetAttribute("IsOn") == true
			_checked[rowComp] = on or nil
			local lastBatch = getLastBatch()
			-- Build origin set (same shape used by both uncheck and re-check).
			local family = getGroupAxes() and AXIS_TO_FAMILY[propKey]
			local originsToRemove = {}
			if family then
				local anySiblingChecked = false
				for _, axis in ipairs(family.all) do
					if axis ~= propKey and _checked[_compKey(sectionTypeName, axis)] then
						anySiblingChecked = true; break
					end
				end
				if not anySiblingChecked then originsToRemove[family.primary] = true end
			else
				originsToRemove[propKey] = true
			end

			if on then
				-- Re-check: move matching retained entries back into _lastBatch so
				-- Apply tracks them under the Randomize waypoint. If the user rolls
				-- next, _rollBatch rebuilds _lastBatch from scratch (overwriting
				-- these entries); if they don't, Apply still commits the live preview
				-- with proper undo coverage instead of silently leaving it untracked.
				if next(originsToRemove) then
					local retained = getOrInitRetainedBatch()
					local target = lastBatch
					for item, itemBatch in pairs(retained) do
						if _itemTypeName[item] == sectionTypeName then
							for axis, entry in pairs(itemBatch) do
								if entry.origin and originsToRemove[entry.origin] then
									if target then
										target[item] = target[item] or {}
										target[item][axis] = entry
									end
									itemBatch[axis] = nil
								end
							end
							if not next(itemBatch) then retained[item] = nil end
						end
					end
				end
			elseif lastBatch and next(originsToRemove) then
				local resetOn = getResetOnUncheck()
				local retained = (not resetOn) and getOrInitRetainedBatch() or nil
				for item, itemBatch in pairs(lastBatch) do
					if _itemTypeName[item] == sectionTypeName then
						for axis, entry in pairs(itemBatch) do
							if entry.origin and originsToRemove[entry.origin] then
								if retained then
									retained[item] = retained[item] or {}
									retained[item][axis] = entry
								end
								itemBatch[axis] = nil
							end
						end
						-- Prune emptied parent so Apply's _batchHasEntries check doesn't
						-- see a phantom item with no writes.
						if not next(itemBatch) then lastBatch[item] = nil end
					end
				end
				if resetOn then
					_restoreSnapshots()
					_replayBatch()
				end
			end
			if _sectionHeaderRefresh[sectionUid] then _sectionHeaderRefresh[sectionUid]() end
			if _typeHeaderRefresh[sectionTypeName] then _typeHeaderRefresh[sectionTypeName]() end
		end)
		table.insert(_toggleConns, conn)
	end

	-- Header tristate cycle: any-on -> all-off, else all-on. Each SetAttribute fires the
	-- corresponding row's IsOn handler which updates _checked + refreshes glyphs.
	local hdrConn = glyph.Activated:Connect(function()
		local anyOn = false
		for _, pk in ipairs(sectionPropsRef) do
			if _checked[_compKey(sectionTypeName, pk)] then anyOn = true; break end
		end
		local target = not anyOn
		for _, pk in ipairs(sectionPropsRef) do
			local t = rowToggles[pk]
			if t then t:SetAttribute("IsOn", target) end
		end
	end)
	table.insert(_toggleConns, hdrConn)
end

return M

--[[
	RandomizerWiring  -  Part-Icles V5 Randomizer System
	Copyright (C) 2026 Qwinkle

	State machine for the modal Randomizer panel.

	Snapshot-preview-apply contract:
	  open(items)  -> snapshot items + FREEZE the item list (selection changes during
	                  preview don't leak writes to non-snapshotted items)
	  rollAll      -> restore snapshots, derive+roll+store batch per frozen item, write
	                  the batch (preview state always reflects fresh roll, no stale)
	  apply        -> Before waypoint, restore snapshots, write last batch once, After
	                  waypoint (history records ONE Apply transaction, not preview writes)
	  cancel/close -> restore snapshots, clear

	Rules.derive runs per item per actual TypeRegistry type. Items are frozen at open
	so preview writes can be restored-and-rerolled atomically. Toggle state listens to
	IsOn AttributeChanged (not stacked Activated) so Widgets.makeToggle's internal flip
	doesn't desync from _checked.
]]

-- Linked-follower detection must use the same sanitizer as the runtime
-- (AxisLinks.sanitize) so the panel agrees with what runtime treats as a follower.
-- Stale/manual bad attrs would otherwise trigger false "mixed link" warnings.
local AxisLinks = require(script.Parent.Parent.Part.AxisLinks)
local RandomizerSection = require(script.Parent.RandomizerSection)
local RandomizerOptions = require(script.Parent.RandomizerOptions)
local Cancel = require(script.Parent.Cancel)
local Selection = game:GetService("Selection")

return function(deps)
	local ctx = deps.ctx
	local panel = deps.panel
	local PropertyCatalog = deps.PropertyCatalog
	local Rules = deps.RandomizerRules
	local Writer = deps.RandomizerWriter
	local QOL = deps.QOL
	local TypeRegistry = deps.TypeRegistry
	local CHS = deps.ChangeHistoryService
	local PE_SECTIONS = deps.PE_SECTIONS or {}
	-- Widgets must be an explicit dep  -  ctx.UIBuilder.Widgets isn't exposed (UIBuilder
	-- doesn't re-export Widgets). Caller passes the module reference.
	local Widgets = deps.Widgets
	-- Theme accessor: caller passes the live theme table from UIBuilder. Fresh read each
	-- time the panel is populated picks up active theme changes.
	local Theme = deps.Theme

	local M = {}

	-- Frozen at open(); never mutated by selection changes during preview.
	local _items = nil           -- array of {item, typeName}
	local _snapshots = nil       -- {[item] = QOL.snapshotItem(item)}
	-- _checked tracks user prop selections for the current open session. Keys are
	-- "TypeName::PropKey" composites so per-type sections track ticks independently.
	local _checked = {}          -- {[compositeKey] = true|nil}
	-- _lastBatch: most recent roll. {[item] = {[propKey] = {value, rule}}}. Apply replays
	-- this against restored snapshots so the final committed state reflects exactly what
	-- the user sees in preview, no stale unchecked props.
	local _lastBatch = nil
	-- Retained batch: entries that were rolled on a checked row, then unchecked while
	-- Reset-on-uncheck was OFF. Survive across Rolls (replayed after snapshot restore
	-- in _rollBatch and _replayBatch) and commit on Apply. Re-checking a row drops its
	-- retained entries so the next Roll generates fresh.
	local _retainedBatch = nil
	local _open = false
	local _toggleConns = {}      -- to disconnect IsOn listeners on close
	-- Tristate section headers + per-section composite-key registry. _sectionProps[
	-- sectionUid] = array of "TypeName::PropKey" composites (sectionUid = typeName::
	-- categoryName), populated during build so header refresh can compute {none/some/
	-- all} state without re-walking PropertyCatalog.
	local _sectionProps = {}
	local _sectionHeaderRefresh = {}  -- {sectionUid -> function()}  -  updates header glyph
	-- Type-level tristate state. typeRowToggles[typeName] = {{comp, toggle}, ...}  - 
	-- collected from every row of every category for that type. Type-glyph click flips all.
	local _typeRowToggles = {}
	local _typeHeaderRefresh = {}  -- {typeName -> function()}  -  updates type glyph

	-- Mixed link-state detection + follower-skip. Both consult AxisLinks.sanitize so the
	-- panel sees the same {follower -> primary or nil} resolution the runtime uses.
	-- Stale/manual bad attrs (cross-group target, chain, cycle) are correctly treated
	-- as "unlinked"  -  runtime ignores them too, and the UI must agree.
	local AXIS_KEYS_LIST = {
		"SizeX", "SizeY", "SizeZ", "RotX", "RotY", "RotZ",
		"RotSpeedX", "RotSpeedY", "RotSpeedZ", "PosX", "PosY", "PosZ",
		"PosOffsetX", "PosOffsetY", "PosOffsetZ",
	}
	local AXIS_PROPS = {}
	for _, k in ipairs(AXIS_KEYS_LIST) do AXIS_PROPS[k] = true end

	-- Group axes magnitude family. When _groupAxes is true (default ON), the roll visits
	-- each axis family at most once per type per Roll All: one base value rolled via the
	-- family's primary (X-axis) prop, then written to X/Y/Z (with linked-follower auto-
	-- promote per item via _writeOrPromote). Off: independent roll per checked axis prop.
	-- Toggle is session-scoped (re-armed to default on open).
	local AXIS_FAMILIES = {
		{primary = "SizeX",      all = {"SizeX", "SizeY", "SizeZ"}},
		{primary = "RotX",       all = {"RotX", "RotY", "RotZ"}},
		{primary = "RotSpeedX",  all = {"RotSpeedX", "RotSpeedY", "RotSpeedZ"}},
		{primary = "PosX",       all = {"PosX", "PosY", "PosZ"}},
		{primary = "PosOffsetX", all = {"PosOffsetX", "PosOffsetY", "PosOffsetZ"}},
	}
	local AXIS_TO_FAMILY = {}
	for _, fam in ipairs(AXIS_FAMILIES) do
		for _, axis in ipairs(fam.all) do AXIS_TO_FAMILY[axis] = fam end
	end
	local _groupAxes = false
	-- When ON, NumberSequence rolls produce 3..7 keypoints and ColorSequence rolls
	-- produce 3..6 palette-honoring keypoints. When OFF, both reduce to a 2-keypoint
	-- roll (start + end)  -  palette still constrains start/end colors. Default OFF  - 
	-- start with the simpler shape.
	local _randomizeKeypoints = false
	-- When ON (default), unchecking a row reverts that prop on the live preview.
	-- When OFF, unchecking just drops the prop from _lastBatch so Apply skips it  -  the
	-- already-rolled visual remains so the user can keep what they rolled while randomizing
	-- something else. Either way, Apply restores snapshots before replay so unchecked
	-- props are NEVER committed.
	local _resetOnUncheck = true
	-- Per-row palette mode override for ColorSequence props. Map from bucketKey (propKey)
	-- to mode name string. Nil / "Auto" entries fall through to the algorithmic weighted
	-- random (RandomizerRules.pickColorMode). Session-scoped  -  re-armed on open(). Mode
	-- change triggers a full _rollBatch so cached buckets invalidate cleanly.
	local _paletteMode = {}

	-- Per-item sanitized link map cache. Populated lazily on first query and reused by
	-- `_hasMixedLinkState` (panel label) and the per-item write path inside `_rollBatch`
	-- (linked-follower auto-promote). Cleared in _teardown + open so stale entries don't
	-- leak into the next session (different selection, possibly different attrs).
	local _resolvedLinks = {}  -- {[item] = AxisLinks.sanitize(raw) | "none"}

	-- Per-type sectioning. _checked is keyed by composite "TypeName::PropKey" so the
	-- panel mirrors Properties' per-type structure  -  checking "Part PosX" doesn't auto-
	-- check "Beam PosX". _itemTypeName mirrors _items for fast item->typeName lookup
	-- inside the uncheck cleanup pass (so we filter _lastBatch by item type when
	-- dropping writes for an unchecked composite).
	local _itemTypeName = {}  -- {[item]=typeName}, populated in open()
	local function _compKey(typeName, propKey) return typeName .. "::" .. propKey end
	local function _splitComp(comp) return comp:match("^(.-)::(.+)$") end

	local function _resolveLinksFor(item)
		local cached = _resolvedLinks[item]
		if cached == "none" then return nil end
		if cached then return cached end
		local config = TypeRegistry.getConfig(item)
		if not config then _resolvedLinks[item] = "none"; return nil end
		local raw = {}
		for _, k in ipairs(AXIS_KEYS_LIST) do raw[k] = config:GetAttribute(k .. "LinkedTo") end
		local resolved = AxisLinks.sanitize(raw)
		_resolvedLinks[item] = resolved
		return resolved
	end

	-- Auto-promote: _rollBatch uses `resolved[axis]` directly inside _writeOrPromote
	-- (per-item write path), so linked followers redirect their write to the primary
	-- axis instead of being silently dropped. Follower-only selection without primary
	-- is honored: a checked SizeY on an item with SizeYLinkedTo=SizeX produces a write
	-- to SizeX with the rolled value, not a no-op.
	-- typeName param so a per-type section's "(mixed link)" annotation only compares
	-- items of that type  -  mixed-link warning is meaningless under per-type sectioning
	-- (each section's checks affect only one type).
	local function _hasMixedLinkState(typeName, propKey)
		if not AXIS_PROPS[propKey] or not _items then return false end
		local linkedSeen, unlinkedSeen = false, false
		for _, e in ipairs(_items) do
			if e.typeName ~= typeName then continue end
			-- Trail items use directAccess (no Configuration)  -  skipped by _resolveLinksFor.
			local resolved = _resolveLinksFor(e.item)
			if resolved then
				if resolved[propKey] ~= nil then linkedSeen = true else unlinkedSeen = true end
				if linkedSeen and unlinkedSeen then return true end
			end
		end
		return false
	end

	-- Reverse-lookup typeName for a TypeRegistry-backed item.
	local function _typeNameFor(item)
		local typeDef = TypeRegistry.getTypeFor(item)
		if not typeDef then return nil end
		for _, name in ipairs(PropertyCatalog.TYPE_NAMES) do
			if TypeRegistry.Types[name] == typeDef then return name end
		end
		return nil
	end

	-- Build {item, typeName} list from current selection. Raw PEs included  - 
	-- RandomizerRules.derive has a PE branch, snapshots via QOL handle native PE props,
	-- Writer routes to native property assignment when rule.nativePE.
	local function _collectFromSelection()
		local list = {}
		for _, item in ipairs(ctx.currentTransformed or {}) do
			local typeName = _typeNameFor(item)
			if typeName then table.insert(list, {item = item, typeName = typeName}) end
		end
		for _, trail in ipairs(ctx.selectedTrails or {}) do
			table.insert(list, {item = trail, typeName = "Trail"})
		end
		for _, pe in ipairs(ctx.selectedPEs or {}) do
			table.insert(list, {item = pe, typeName = "PE"})
		end
		-- BeamNative (plain Beam, directAccess) intentionally excluded: no graph / axis props
		-- to randomize. Promote via Transform → emitter Beam to get randomizable graphs.
		return list
	end

	-- Scoped restore. Reverts only props Randomizer wrote (tracked via _lastBatch +
	-- _retainedBatch) so manual edits made via the Property panel while Randomizer
	-- was open survive Roll / Apply / SelectionChanged. Same data-loss-safe path
	-- M.cancel uses; routes through Modules/Randomizer/Cancel.luau.
	local function _restoreSnapshots()
		if not _snapshots then return end
		Cancel.restoreTouchedOnly({
			snapshots = _snapshots,
			lastBatch = _lastBatch,
			retainedBatch = _retainedBatch,
			QOL = QOL,
		})
	end

	-- Nested itemBatch may end up empty after uncheck/re-check pruning; check inner
	-- tables instead of just the outer key set.
	local function _batchHasEntries(batch)
		if not batch then return false end
		for _, itemBatch in pairs(batch) do if next(itemBatch) then return true end end
		return false
	end

	-- Replay retained then _lastBatch against restored snapshots. Last-write-wins on
	-- overlap so a fresh roll overwrites its previously-retained entry.
	local function _writeBatch(batch)
		if not batch then return end
		for item, itemBatch in pairs(batch) do
			if item.Parent then
				for propKey, entry in pairs(itemBatch) do
					Writer.write(item, propKey, entry.value, entry.rule)
				end
			end
		end
	end
	local function _replayBatch() _writeBatch(_retainedBatch); _writeBatch(_lastBatch) end

	-- Compute a fresh batch + apply preview writes. Restores snapshots first so Roll
	-- always start from the original baseline; only checked props get fresh values. Unchecked
	-- props stay at their snapshot values (no stale leftovers from previous rolls).
	-- Multi-selection coordination. _rollBatch is split into two phases:
	--   Phase 1  -  roll once per (typeName, bucketKey) bucket. bucketKey is family.primary
	--             when groupAxes is on AND propKey is in an axis family, else propKey itself.
	--             rolls cached so item B reuses the value rolled for item A's same bucket
	--             (independent-per-item rolling is not currently supported).
	--   Phase 2  -  per item, walk checked props (or families when grouped). For each axis,
	--             apply linked-follower auto-promote: if the item has the axis linked to a
	--             primary, write the primary instead with the rolled value. Skip absent
	--             props per type (Attachment lacks SizeX/Y/Z, etc.).
	-- _lastBatch records the literal (axis -> {value, rule}) writes done so Apply replays
	-- exactly the same writes (incl. promoted primaries).
	local function _rollBatch()
		if not _items or not _snapshots then return end
		-- Clear the resolved-link cache so AxisLink edits made in the Properties
		-- panel between rolls take effect on the next roll.
		_resolvedLinks = {}
		_restoreSnapshots()
		-- Replay retained (Reset-on-uncheck-OFF) entries first so pinned values stay
		-- visible. Then generate fresh _lastBatch for currently-checked composites;
		-- new writes overwrite retained ones if the same prop ends up in both.
		_writeBatch(_retainedBatch)
		_lastBatch = {}

		-- Phase 1 caches: (typeName, bucketKey) -> {value, rule} or false (rule absent).
		-- Do NOT early-reject when propDef is nil. Virtual emit attrs (EmitCount/EmitDelay/
		-- EmitDuration) live as item-level attributes  -  they have no entry in TypeRegistry.
		-- properties. RandomizerRules.derive handles them via the override.virtualEmitAttr
		-- branch in _decorateOverride (returns a scalar rule with the virtualEmitAttr flag
		-- set so RandomizerWriter dispatches via item:SetAttribute).
		local rolledBuckets = {}
		local function _ensureBucketRoll(typeName, bucketKey)
			rolledBuckets[typeName] = rolledBuckets[typeName] or {}
			local cache = rolledBuckets[typeName]
			local cached = cache[bucketKey]
			if cached ~= nil then return cached or nil end
			local typeDef = TypeRegistry.Types[typeName]
			local propDef = typeDef and typeDef.properties and typeDef.properties[bucketKey]
			-- Pass propDef even when nil; derive's virtualEmitAttr branch doesn't need it.
			local rule = Rules.derive(typeName, bucketKey, propDef)
			if not rule then cache[bucketKey] = false; return nil end
			-- Palette mode is keyed by composite (typeName::propKey) so per-type rows
			-- pick their own palette without cross-talk.
			if rule.colorSequence and _paletteMode[_compKey(typeName, bucketKey)] then
				rule.paletteMode = _paletteMode[_compKey(typeName, bucketKey)]
			end
			-- Stamp the keypoint-count toggle onto the rule so NumberSequence /
			-- ColorSequence rollers can fall back to the simpler 2-keypoint shape when off.
			rule.randomizeKeypoints = _randomizeKeypoints
			local value = Rules.roll(rule)
			if value == nil then cache[bucketKey] = false; return nil end
			local entry = {value = value, rule = rule}
			cache[bucketKey] = entry
			return entry
		end

		-- Families touched are per-typeName (composite-key _checked). Item B of type
		-- Beam shouldn't have its X/Y/Z rolled because user checked Part SizeX.
		local familyTouchedByType = {}  -- {[typeName]={[primary]=true}}
		if _groupAxes then
			for comp, on in pairs(_checked) do
				if on then
					local tn, pk = _splitComp(comp)
					if tn and pk and AXIS_TO_FAMILY[pk] then
						familyTouchedByType[tn] = familyTouchedByType[tn] or {}
						familyTouchedByType[tn][AXIS_TO_FAMILY[pk].primary] = true
					end
				end
			end
		end

		for _, e in ipairs(_items) do
			if not e.item.Parent then continue end
			local itemBatch = {}
			local typeName = e.typeName
			local typeDef = TypeRegistry.Types[typeName]
			local resolved = _resolveLinksFor(e.item)
			-- Collect this type's checked propKeys (drop other types' composites).
			local typeChecked = {}  -- {[propKey]=true}
			for comp, on in pairs(_checked) do
				if on then
					local tn, pk = _splitComp(comp)
					if tn == typeName and pk then typeChecked[pk] = true end
				end
			end
			-- Skip the per-item write loops entirely when nothing is checked for this type.
			if not next(typeChecked) then continue end

			-- Write a single (item, axis, entry) honoring linked-follower auto-promote,
			-- absent-prop guard, and direct-vs-promoted ordering. `origin` records which
			-- checked propKey (or family.primary
			-- in grouped mode) initiated the write  -  drives the uncheck cleanup pass. Virtual
			-- emit attrs (entry.rule.virtualEmitAttr) bypass the absent-prop guard AND the
			-- link-promotion path (item-level attrs, AxisLinks doesn't apply).
			--
			-- mode:
			--   "any"       -  write target = resolved follower (if any) else axis (used by
			--                grouped path where family.all iterates primary-first, so
			--                ordering is deterministic).
			--   "direct"    -  skip linked followers entirely (Pass 1 of ungrouped). Direct
			--                check writes its own axis. Linked-follower writes are deferred
			--                to Pass 2 so direct check always wins ownership of the target.
			--   "promoted"  -  only writes linked followers, AND only if the promoted target
			--                is still absent in itemBatch (Pass 2 of ungrouped).
			local function _writeOrPromote(axis, origin, entry, mode)
				mode = mode or "any"
				local isVirtual = entry.rule and entry.rule.virtualEmitAttr
				-- nativePE bypass mirrors virtualEmitAttr  -  PE has no TypeRegistry entry,
				-- so the absent-prop guard would reject every PE write. Rules.derive
				-- already validated the prop via PE_PROP_TYPES upstream.
				local isNativePE = entry.rule and entry.rule.nativePE
				if not isVirtual and not isNativePE
					and not (typeDef and typeDef.properties and typeDef.properties[axis]) then
					return
				end
				local link = (not isVirtual) and (not isNativePE) and resolved and resolved[axis] or nil
				if mode == "direct" and link then return end
				if mode == "promoted" and (isVirtual or not link) then return end
				local target
				if isVirtual then
					target = axis
				elseif link and (mode == "any" or mode == "promoted") then
					target = link
				else
					target = axis
				end
				if itemBatch[target] then return end
				itemBatch[target] = {value = entry.value, rule = entry.rule, origin = origin}
				Writer.write(e.item, target, entry.value, entry.rule)
			end

			if _groupAxes then
				-- Grouped: families with any checked axis roll ONCE per family per type.
				-- All 3 axes in family.all share the rolled value (subject to absent-prop
				-- skip + linked-follower auto-promote per item). Origin = family.primary so
				-- a later uncheck of the LAST family axis can find + drop these entries.
				local typeFamilies = familyTouchedByType[typeName] or {}
				for primary, _ in pairs(typeFamilies) do
					local family = AXIS_TO_FAMILY[primary]
					local entry = _ensureBucketRoll(typeName, primary)
					if entry then
						for _, axis in ipairs(family.all) do _writeOrPromote(axis, primary, entry) end
					end
				end
				-- Non-axis checked props share the bucket model too. Origin = propKey.
				for propKey, _on in pairs(typeChecked) do
					if not AXIS_TO_FAMILY[propKey] then
						local entry = _ensureBucketRoll(typeName, propKey)
						if entry then _writeOrPromote(propKey, propKey, entry) end
					end
				end
			else
				-- Ungrouped: every checked prop rolls into its own bucket. Auto-promote
				-- still applies  -  a checked follower writes the primary for that item.
				-- Origin = propKey (the checked source), even when the WRITE target is a
				-- different prop due to follower promotion.
				--
				-- Two-pass for direct vs promoted determinism. If SizeX and SizeY are both
				-- checked AND item has SizeYLinkedTo=SizeX, both want to target SizeX.
				-- pairs() ordering is nondeterministic  -  first-write-wins could let the
				-- follower-promoted SizeY value beat the direct SizeX value. Pass 1 writes
				-- directly (allowPromote=false), Pass 2 promotes only if the target is
				-- still absent. Direct check beats promotion every time.
				for propKey, _on in pairs(typeChecked) do
					local entry = _ensureBucketRoll(typeName, propKey)
					if entry then _writeOrPromote(propKey, propKey, entry, "direct") end
				end
				for propKey, _on in pairs(typeChecked) do
					local entry = _ensureBucketRoll(typeName, propKey)
					if entry then _writeOrPromote(propKey, propKey, entry, "promoted") end
				end
			end

			if next(itemBatch) then _lastBatch[e.item] = itemBatch end
		end
	end

	-- Set-equality guard  -  Studio's UI can briefly clear and restore Selection during
	-- a click; we only reinit when the effective items table actually differs. Compares
	-- by item identity AND typeName so a re-classification (e.g. type swap on the same
	-- instance) still triggers a refresh.
	local function _sameItems(a, b)
		if not a or not b or #a ~= #b then return false end
		local seen = {}
		for _, e in ipairs(a) do seen[e.item] = e.typeName end
		for _, e in ipairs(b) do
			if seen[e.item] ~= e.typeName then return false end
			seen[e.item] = nil
		end
		return true
	end

	-- Shared (re)initialization for items + snapshots. Accepts optional pre-collected
	-- items list so SelectionChanged callers don't collect twice.
	-- Selection delta filter: composite keys are "TypeName::PropKey". When the
	-- selection changes, only drop entries whose TypeName no longer appears in
	-- the new selection  -  ticks on still-present types must survive so the user
	-- doesn't lose state by extending the selection.
	local function _reinitFromSelection(precollected)
		_restoreSnapshots()
		local items = precollected or _collectFromSelection()
		_items = items
		_snapshots = {}
		_itemTypeName = {}
		local typeNamesPresent = {}
		for _, e in ipairs(_items) do
			_snapshots[e.item] = QOL.snapshotItem(e.item)
			_itemTypeName[e.item] = e.typeName
			typeNamesPresent[e.typeName] = true
		end
		_lastBatch = nil
		_retainedBatch = nil
		_resolvedLinks = {}
		for compositeKey in pairs(_checked) do
			local typeName = compositeKey:match("^([^:]+)::")
			if not (typeName and typeNamesPresent[typeName]) then _checked[compositeKey] = nil end
		end
		for compositeKey in pairs(_paletteMode) do
			local typeName = compositeKey:match("^([^:]+)::")
			if not (typeName and typeNamesPresent[typeName]) then _paletteMode[compositeKey] = nil end
		end
	end

	-- Live selection refresh. Disconnected on teardown.
	local _selectionConn = nil

	function M.open()
		if _open then return end -- prevent double-open
		-- Open even when the selection has no transformed items. Empty panel is an OK
		-- parked state; the user can refine selection and reopen when ready.
		_snapshots = nil  -- ensure _reinitFromSelection's restore is a no-op on first init
		_reinitFromSelection()
		-- Group axes defaults ON. Each session opens with the toggle armed; user opts
		-- OUT if they want independent per-axis rolls. _checked / _paletteMode /
		-- _resolvedLinks already cleared by _reinitFromSelection.
		_groupAxes = true
		_randomizeKeypoints = false
		_resetOnUncheck = true
		_open = true
		M.populateSections()
		panel.panel.Visible = true
		-- Defer the listener body. RBXScriptSignal connection order isn't guaranteed,
		-- so without defer this listener can fire before the plugin's main selection
		-- listener has refreshed ctx.currentTransformed  -  leaving the panel one step
		-- behind the user's actual selection (e.g. select 2 → no change, select 3 →
		-- shows "2 selected"). Defer to the next resumption so handleSelection has
		-- finished updating ctx before we read it.
		if _selectionConn then _selectionConn:Disconnect() end
		_selectionConn = Selection.SelectionChanged:Connect(function()
			task.defer(function()
				if not _open then return end
				local nextItems = _collectFromSelection()
				if _sameItems(_items or {}, nextItems) then return end
				_reinitFromSelection(nextItems)
				M.populateSections()
			end)
		end)
	end

	function M.rollAll() _rollBatch() end

	function M.apply()
		if not _open then return end
		-- Skip waypoints when both batches are empty. Walks nested itemBatch tables
		-- since `next()` on the outer table alone passes for `{[item]={}}`.
		if not _batchHasEntries(_lastBatch) and not _batchHasEntries(_retainedBatch) then
			M._teardown()
			return
		end
		CHS:SetWaypoint("Part-Icles: Before Randomize")
		-- Restore baseline + replay both retained AND last batches atomically so undo
		-- captures one diff and so retained pinned values commit alongside fresh rolls.
		_restoreSnapshots()
		_replayBatch()
		CHS:SetWaypoint("Part-Icles: Randomize")
		M._teardown()
	end

	function M.cancel()
		if not _open then return end
		-- Scoped restore (Modules/Randomizer/Cancel.luau): only revert props the
		-- Randomizer wrote during this open session, so unrelated edits survive.
		Cancel.restoreTouchedOnly({
			snapshots = _snapshots,
			lastBatch = _lastBatch,
			retainedBatch = _retainedBatch,
			QOL = QOL,
		})
		M._teardown()
	end

	-- Palette dropdown's expanded options frame parents to ScreenGui (escapes ScrollingFrame
	-- clipping); hiding the panel doesn't destroy it. AND makeDropdown toggles the ancestor
	-- ScrollingFrame's `ScrollingEnabled` on MouseEnter/Leave so MouseWheel only cycles
	-- dropdown options instead of scrolling the section list  -  if populate or teardown fires
	-- while the cursor is on the dropdown, MouseLeave never runs and the scroll stays stuck.
	-- Helper pairs the dismiss with the defensive restore so both call sites (populateSections
	-- and _teardown) stay in sync.
	local function _closeDropdownUi()
		if Widgets.hideDropdownExpansion then Widgets.hideDropdownExpansion() end
		if panel.sectionList then panel.sectionList.ScrollingEnabled = true end
	end

	function M._teardown()
		_snapshots = nil
		_items = nil
		_itemTypeName = {}
		_lastBatch = nil
		_retainedBatch = nil
		_checked = {}
		_open = false
		for _, conn in ipairs(_toggleConns) do conn:Disconnect() end
		_toggleConns = {}
		_resolvedLinks = {}  -- clear sanitized-link cache so next open re-reads attrs
		-- Drop the SelectionChanged hook so closed panels stop reacting.
		if _selectionConn then _selectionConn:Disconnect(); _selectionConn = nil end
		_closeDropdownUi()
		panel.panel.Visible = false
		-- A minimized panel has a tray chip; the session it would reopen is gone.
		if Widgets.restoreChip then Widgets.restoreChip(panel.panel) end
	end

	-- Read accessor for UI populate. Takes (typeName, propKey)  -  composite key.
	function M.isChecked(typeName, propKey) return _checked[_compKey(typeName, propKey)] == true end
	-- Read accessor so toolbar can branch open/cancel.
	function M.isOpen() return _open end

	-- Recompute a section header's tristate glyph from current _checked. Called whenever any
	-- contained-row toggle flips OR when the user clicks the header itself.
	local function _refreshHeaderGlyph(sectionName, glyphLabel)
		local props = _sectionProps[sectionName]
		if not props or #props == 0 then glyphLabel.Text = "[ ]"; return end
		local on = 0
		for _, k in ipairs(props) do if _checked[k] then on = on + 1 end end
		if on == 0 then glyphLabel.Text = "[ ]"
		elseif on == #props then glyphLabel.Text = "[X]"
		else glyphLabel.Text = "[~]" end
	end

	-- Build sectionList. Listens for IsOn AttributeChanged on each Widgets.makeToggle so
	-- _checked stays in sync without stacking another Activated handler.
	-- UI polish:
	--   - Tristate section headers via a TextButton glyph ([ ] / [~] / [X]). Click cycles
	--     all-or-none (off if any-on, else on for every prop in the section).
	--   - Mixed link-state qualifier appended to axis-prop row labels when items in the
	--     frozen selection disagree on link state.
	function M.populateSections()
		-- Rebuilding rows must dismiss any open palette dropdown AND restore the section
		-- ScrollingFrame's `ScrollingEnabled` (in case populate fires while cursor is on
		-- the dropdown  -  same edge case as _teardown). _closeDropdownUi pairs both.
		_closeDropdownUi()
		for _, child in ipairs(panel.sectionList:GetChildren()) do
			if child:IsA("TextLabel") or child:IsA("Frame") then child:Destroy() end
		end
		for _, conn in ipairs(_toggleConns) do conn:Disconnect() end
		_toggleConns = {}
		_sectionProps = {}
		_sectionHeaderRefresh = {}
		_typeRowToggles = {}
		_typeHeaderRefresh = {}
		-- Tree-style sections  -  top-level type header ("TypeName (N selected)") with
		-- category sub-headers (Spawning / Appearance / ...) underneath. Mirrors
		-- Properties panel hierarchy. typesInSel gates `randomizableSectionsByType` so
		-- other types' props don't render. countByType drives the per-type-header count.
		local typesInSel = {}
		local countByType = {}
		if _items then
			for _, e in ipairs(_items) do
				typesInSel[e.typeName] = true
				countByType[e.typeName] = (countByType[e.typeName] or 0) + 1
			end
		end
		local sections = PropertyCatalog.randomizableSectionsByType(TypeRegistry, PE_SECTIONS, Rules, typesInSel)
		local Th = Theme
		local W = Widgets

		-- Session option rows (Group axes / keypoint count / reset on uncheck) live in RandomizerOptions.
		RandomizerOptions.emit({
			W = W, Th = Th, sectionList = panel.sectionList, toggleConns = _toggleConns,
			getGroupAxes = function() return _groupAxes end,
			setGroupAxes = function(on) _groupAxes = on end,
			getRandomizeKeypoints = function() return _randomizeKeypoints end,
			setRandomizeKeypoints = function(on) _randomizeKeypoints = on end,
			getResetOnUncheck = function() return _resetOnUncheck end,
			setResetOnUncheck = function(on) _resetOnUncheck = on end,
			hasRetained = function() return _retainedBatch ~= nil end,
			clearRetained = function() _retainedBatch = nil end,
			hasLastBatch = function() return _lastBatch ~= nil end,
			restoreSnapshots = _restoreSnapshots, rollBatch = _rollBatch, replayBatch = _replayBatch,
		})

		-- Bucket sections by typeName so we can emit a top-level type header once per
		-- type, then list that type's category sub-sections beneath it.
		local sectionsByType = {}
		local typeOrder = {}
		for _, sec in ipairs(sections) do
			if not sectionsByType[sec.typeName] then
				sectionsByType[sec.typeName] = {}
				table.insert(typeOrder, sec.typeName)
			end
			table.insert(sectionsByType[sec.typeName], sec)
		end
		for _, typeName in ipairs(typeOrder) do
			-- Type group is wrapped in a TypeContainer Frame so the type-level collapse
			-- arrow can hide everything beneath the type header in one flip. Container
			-- holds {typeHdr, typeChildren}. typeChildren holds all category section
			-- blobs + their sectionBody Frames. Collapse arrow on typeHdr toggles
			-- typeChildren visibility.
			local typeContainer = Instance.new("Frame")
			typeContainer.Name = "TypeContainer_"..typeName
			typeContainer.BackgroundTransparency = 1
			typeContainer.AutomaticSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.Y
			typeContainer.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 0)
			typeContainer.Parent = panel.sectionList
			W.addListLayout(typeContainer, 4, Enum.FillDirection.Vertical)

			local typeHdr = W.makeBlob("Type_"..typeName, typeContainer, UDim2.new(1, -8, 0, 26))
			W.addPadding(typeHdr, 4, 4, 0, 0)
			-- Type-level tristate glyph (parent of all categories' rows for this type).
			local typeGlyph = Instance.new("TextButton")
			typeGlyph.Name = "TypeGlyph"
			typeGlyph.BackgroundTransparency = 1
			typeGlyph.Text = "[ ]"
			typeGlyph.Font = Th.Font; typeGlyph.TextSize = 12; typeGlyph.TextColor3 = Th.BrightGold
			typeGlyph.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left
			-- Tighter glyph spacing  -  bracket text only takes ~14px so a 28px box left
			-- huge gaps between [ ] and the label. Drop to 16px.
			typeGlyph.Position = UDim2.new(0, 16, 0, 0); typeGlyph.Size = UDim2.new(0, 16, 1, 0)
			typeGlyph.Parent = typeHdr
			-- Friendly display name from TypeRegistry uiSection. PE has no TypeRegistry
			-- entry (raw ParticleEmitter); BuildProperties banners it as "Particles"  - 
			-- mirror that here.
			local typeDef0 = TypeRegistry.Types[typeName]
			local displayName = (typeDef0 and typeDef0.uiSection)
				or (typeName == "PE" and "Particles")
				or typeName
			local typeLbl = W.makeLabel("L", typeHdr,
				("%s (%d selected)"):format(displayName, countByType[typeName] or 0),
				Th.BrightGold, Th.Font, 12)
			typeLbl.Position = UDim2.new(0, 34, 0, 0)
			typeLbl.Size = UDim2.new(1, -38, 1, 0)
			typeLbl.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left

			local typeChildren = Instance.new("Frame")
			typeChildren.Name = "TypeChildren_"..typeName
			typeChildren.BackgroundTransparency = 1
			typeChildren.AutomaticSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.Y
			typeChildren.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 0)
			typeChildren.Parent = typeContainer
			W.addListLayout(typeChildren, 4, Enum.FillDirection.Vertical)
			-- Left-indent so categories visually nest under their type header.
			W.addPadding(typeChildren, 12, 0, 0, 0)
			W.addCollapseButton(typeHdr, {typeChildren}, {anchorLeft = true, arrowPos = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 0)})

			_typeRowToggles[typeName] = {}
			local typeNameRef = typeName
			local typeGlyphRef = typeGlyph
			_typeHeaderRefresh[typeName] = function()
				local lst = _typeRowToggles[typeNameRef]
				if not lst or #lst == 0 then typeGlyphRef.Text = "[ ]"; return end
				local on = 0
				for _, e in ipairs(lst) do if _checked[e.comp] then on = on + 1 end end
				typeGlyphRef.Text = (on == 0 and "[ ]") or (on == #lst and "[X]") or "[~]"
			end
			local typeGlyphConn = typeGlyph.Activated:Connect(function()
				local lst = _typeRowToggles[typeNameRef]
				if not lst then return end
				local anyOn = false
				for _, e in ipairs(lst) do if _checked[e.comp] then anyOn = true; break end end
				local target = not anyOn
				for _, e in ipairs(lst) do e.toggle:SetAttribute("IsOn", target) end
			end)
			table.insert(_toggleConns, typeGlyphConn)

			-- Per-section emission extracted to RandomizerSection sibling. Pass the bag
			-- of shared mutable refs + helpers; mutable scalars come through getters so
			-- the section's row closures see live values.
			local sectionBag = {
				W = W, Th = Th, TypeRegistry = TypeRegistry, Rules = Rules,
				checked = _checked, paletteMode = _paletteMode, itemTypeName = _itemTypeName,
				sectionProps = _sectionProps, sectionHeaderRefresh = _sectionHeaderRefresh,
				typeRowToggles = _typeRowToggles, typeHeaderRefresh = _typeHeaderRefresh,
				toggleConns = _toggleConns, AXIS_TO_FAMILY = AXIS_TO_FAMILY, compKey = _compKey,
				hasMixedLinkState = _hasMixedLinkState, refreshHeaderGlyph = _refreshHeaderGlyph,
				restoreSnapshots = _restoreSnapshots, replayBatch = _replayBatch, rollBatch = _rollBatch,
				getLastBatch = function() return _lastBatch end,
				getGroupAxes = function() return _groupAxes end,
				getResetOnUncheck = function() return _resetOnUncheck end,
				getOrInitRetainedBatch = function()
					_retainedBatch = _retainedBatch or {}
					return _retainedBatch
				end,
			}
			for _, sec in ipairs(sectionsByType[typeName]) do
				local sectionUid = _compKey(sec.typeName, sec.name)
				RandomizerSection.emit(sectionBag, sec, sec.typeName, sectionUid, sec.name, typeChildren)
			end
		end
		-- Empty-selection hint blob: distinguishes "empty" from "loading" when no
		-- type sections render. Non-interactive; follows the row blob convention.
		if #typeOrder == 0 then
			local emptyBlob = W.makeBlob("EmptyHint", panel.sectionList, UDim2.new(1, -8, 0, 22))
			W.addPadding(emptyBlob, 8, 4, 0, 0)
			local emptyLbl = W.makeLabel("L", emptyBlob,
				"No transformed items selected", Th.DarkGold, Th.Font, 10)
			emptyLbl.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left
		end
	end

	return M
end

--[[
	RandomizerWriter  -  Part-Icles V5
	Copyright (C) 2026 Qwinkle

	Per-prop write dispatch for the Randomizer:

	- Virtual emit attrs (`virtualEmitAttr = true` in rule) -> `item:SetAttribute(propKey, value)`
	  because EmitCount/EmitDelay/EmitDuration live on the item, NOT in PartIcleProperties.
	- Everything else -> `TypeRegistry.write(item, propKey, value)` so attrName / nonNegative
	  / directAccess Trail dispatch all happen via the existing TypeRegistry pipeline.
	- For graph (NumberSequence / ColorSequence) writes, ALSO clear the `<propKey>_BezierHandles`
	  attribute on the Configuration. Old handles don't match new keypoints; leaving them in
	  place would make the Graph editor open with junk on next select.
]]

local TypeRegistry = require(script.Parent.Parent.Part.TypeRegistry)

local RandomizerWriter = {}

-- Per-rule write dispatch. Caller threads the rule from RandomizerRules.derive(...) so the
-- writer doesn't have to re-derive.
function RandomizerWriter.write(item, propKey, value, rule)
	if rule and rule.virtualEmitAttr then
		-- Item-level attribute; not in PartIcleProperties Configuration.
		pcall(function() item:SetAttribute(propKey, value) end)
		return
	end
	-- Native PE write  -  direct property assignment on the ParticleEmitter instance.
	-- PE has no Configuration child / TypeRegistry entry; props live as native
	-- ParticleEmitter members (Rate / Lifetime / Color / etc).
	if rule and rule.nativePE then
		local nativeOk = pcall(function() item[propKey] = value end)
		-- Clear stale Bezier handle JSON on the PE itself for graph rolls.
		-- Without this, GraphEditor._load() can resurrect the pre-randomize
		-- curve from the leftover handles instead of showing the new keypoints.
		if nativeOk and (rule.numberSequence or rule.colorSequence) then
			pcall(function() item:SetAttribute(propKey .. "_BezierHandles", nil) end)
		end
		return
	end
	-- stringForm rules (e.g. Trail Duration) store as a string; generator returns a number,
	-- writer tostring-wraps before TypeRegistry.write so the underlying string-attr accepts.
	local writeValue = value
	if rule and rule.stringForm and type(value) == "number" then
		writeValue = tostring(value)
	end
	-- TypeRegistry handles attrName overrides (BeamBrightness/PLRange/ImgFlipbookFramerate),
	-- nonNegative clamping, directAccess Trail native-property writes, and Configuration
	-- attribute writes for everything else. Wrapped in pcall so a single bad write doesn't
	-- abort a multi-prop Roll All.
	local writeOk = pcall(function() TypeRegistry.write(item, propKey, writeValue) end)

	-- Graph writes: clear stored Bezier handles ONLY after a successful TypeRegistry write.
	-- Otherwise a bad write would leave the prior valid graph in place but delete its handles.
	-- Handles attr is keyed by the LOGICAL prop key (matches the existing graph connector
	-- convention), not the attrName override.
	if writeOk and rule and (rule.numberSequence or rule.colorSequence) then
		-- Bezier handle attribute lives on the Configuration when one exists; on
		-- the item itself for raw ParticleEmitter / directAccess Trail.
		local target = TypeRegistry.getConfig(item) or item
		pcall(function() target:SetAttribute(propKey .. "_BezierHandles", nil) end)
	end
end

-- Convenience: write a batch of {[propKey] = {value, rule}} entries on one item. Useful for
-- the Randomize panel's apply path (Roll All -> snapshot per item -> writeBatch per item).
function RandomizerWriter.writeBatch(item, batch)
	for propKey, entry in pairs(batch) do
		RandomizerWriter.write(item, propKey, entry.value, entry.rule)
	end
end

return RandomizerWriter
